info.title: Core System API
info.description: Enterprise Core System — capacités transverses (identity, ledger, wallet) exposées à plusieurs produits. Authentification par API key (`Authorization: Bearer pk_<env>_<id>.<secret>`), voir `GET /v1/whoami`.

get.description:
Resolves the bearer API key and returns which Project it belongs to,
in which environment (sandbox/live), and which scopes it carries. The
first call an integrating product should make to confirm its
credentials.

post.description:
Requires the `notifications:write` scope and an `Idempotency-Key`
header (spec §13). `to_party_ref` is a correlation reference only
— resolving it to an actual delivery address is a provider adapter
concern, not the Core's (ADR-0041 §5).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Caller-supplied unique key used for both the HTTP-level response cache and the use case's own duplicate-effect guard. Same key + same body = cached response, never a second effect. Same key + different body = 409. See ADR-0025 (idempotency design) and G7 (mandatory on every monetary mutation route).

post.description:
The request names only a `channel` (e.g. `mtn_momo`, `card`), never a
provider — `StartPaymentUseCase` resolves which adapter actually
handles it via the Project's routing configuration (ADR-0038 §2).
Requires the `payments:write` scope and an `Idempotency-Key` header
(G7, ADR-0025). Crediting a wallet on success is never implicit — it
only happens if `wallet_recipient_external_ref` is given (ADR-0037).
Prefer `POST /v1/payments/paylink` or `POST /v1/payments/payin`
for new integrations.

get.description:
Reads the Core's own last-known state only — no live call to the
provider. Requires the `payments:read` scope, and returns the same
not-found response whether the payment doesn't exist or belongs to
another project.

idempotency_key.description:
Review finding, user-directed: this is the documented
fallback truth source when a webhook is missed — it must
hand back the same caller-supplied context the webhook
already does (its own Idempotency-Key, and the callback_url
it registered), or polling here loses information the
webhook has.

PaymentFlow.description: Discriminates between the two payment initiation flows exposed by aggregator-style providers. `Payin` is the synchronous, app-driven flow (used by mobile apps and server-to-server integrations that drive the customer through their own UX). MyCoolPay exposes this as `POST /payin`; CinetPay exposes it as `POST /v2/payment`; MTN exposes it as `POST /collection/.../requesttopay`.  `Paylink` is the hosted-link, redirect-driven flow (used by web apps that hand the customer off to a provider-hosted page). MyCoolPay exposes this as `POST /paylink`; CinetPay returns a `payment_url` alongside the same initiation call (the discriminator is implicit).  Providers that do not distinguish the two flows (e.g. CinetPay) treat `Payin` as the default and ignore the discriminator on the `InitiatePaymentCommand`.
PaymentFlow.title: PaymentFlow

RegisterWebhookEndpointRequest.description:
Validates `POST /v1/webhook-endpoints`. The `webhooks:write` scope
is enforced in the controller against the calling Project.

url.description:
The public URL the Core POSTs the signed payload to
when an event matches. Must be reachable from the
Core's outbound network — no localhost, no
RFC-1918 ranges, no link-local addresses. The
reason is that a registered endpoint is retried
automatically for hours, so an address that points
at an internal service today could become an
unintentional exfiltration channel tomorrow. HTTPS
is required in production; HTTP is accepted only
for local development.

events.description:
The list of event types the endpoint wants to
receive. At least one entry is required. Use the
wildcard `["*"]` to subscribe to every event the
Core emits — useful for development, but avoid in
production because new event types are added
silently to wildcard subscribers and may break a
receiver that expected a fixed schema.

items.description:
One event type per array element. The currently
supported values are listed in the enum of this
field in `/docs/api`.

RegisterWebhookEndpointRequest.title: RegisterWebhookEndpointRequest

phone_number.description:
The phone number of the WhatsApp device that will
display the pairing code, in international format
(E.164, e.g. `+2376XXXXXXXX`). The Core forwards
this value to the channel provider as the device
identifier for the linking flow. It is not stored
by the Core — the provider is the source of truth
for the session.

channel.description:
The channel the file will be sent through. See
`POST /v1/notifications/text` for the full
description; the rule is the same across all three
content types.

to_party_ref.description:
Opaque recipient reference in YOUR system. Same
semantics as `to_party_ref` on
`POST /v1/notifications/text`.

media_url.description:
Publicly reachable HTTP(S) URL of the file. The
provider fetches it server-side and re-hosts it.
Must be reachable from the provider's outbound
network (no private IPs, no localhost) — same
constraint as `POST /v1/webhook-endpoints`.

filename.description:
The filename the recipient sees and the
content-disposition header is built from. The file's
actual content is fetched from `media_url`.

mimetype.description:
The MIME type of the file
(`application/pdf`, `image/png`,
`application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`...).
Required because file extensions are not reliable
signals — the provider uses this to set
`Content-Type` when re-uploading.

caption.description:
Optional text rendered above the file in the
recipient's client (most chat platforms support a
short text + file combo). UTF-8. Provider length
limits apply.

variables.description:
Free-form data the provider needs to actually
deliver the message. Shape is provider-specific —
for WhatsApp via WAHA, the recipient phone number
travels here as `variables.phone_number`.

to_party_ref.description:
Opaque recipient reference in YOUR system. Same
semantics as `to_party_ref` on
`POST /v1/notifications/text` — the Core does not
resolve it; the provider adapter does, using
`variables.phone_number` and the channel's expected
addressing scheme.

media_url.description:
Publicly reachable HTTP(S) URL of the image. The
provider fetches it server-side and re-hosts it, so
you do not upload binary. The URL must be reachable
from the provider's outbound network (no private
IPs, no localhost) — this is the same constraint as
`POST /v1/webhook-endpoints`.

caption.description:
Optional text rendered alongside the image in the
recipient's client. UTF-8. Provider length limits
apply.

filename.description:
Optional filename hint the provider uses when the
image is forwarded as a file attachment.

mimetype.description:
Optional MIME type of the image. When omitted, the
provider infers it from the URL extension or the
upstream `Content-Type` header.

variables.description:
Free-form data the provider needs to actually deliver
the message. Shape is provider-specific — for
WhatsApp via WAHA, the recipient phone number
travels here as `variables.phone_number`.

channel.description:
The channel the message will be sent through. The Core
picks the right provider based on this value and the
calling Project's configuration. Adding a new channel
is a configuration change, never a code change —
check `/docs/api` for the current list.

to_party_ref.description:
An opaque reference that identifies the recipient in
YOUR system — a user id, an order id, a customer
record id. NOT a phone number and NOT an email
address: the Core does not know how to reach the
recipient from this value alone. How it gets mapped to
a real delivery address depends on the channel and
provider — typically by reading a field like
`variables.phone_number` you include below.

text.description:
The message body, UTF-8. Rendered verbatim by the
provider — the Core does not interpolate
`variables` into it. Provider-specific length limits
apply downstream (check the channel's adapter
documentation for the cap on the platform you target).
examples: Hello Marie, your order #1234 is confirmed.

variables.description:
Free-form data the provider needs to actually deliver
the message. Shape and required fields are
provider-specific — for WhatsApp via WAHA, the
recipient phone number travels here as
`variables.phone_number`. The Core forwards the
array as-is and never inspects it; see the channel's
adapter docs for what to include.

StartPaymentRequest.description:
Validates `POST /v1/payments`. The `payments:write` scope is enforced
in the controller against the calling Project — this class only
validates payload shape.

Two headers sit above this body and are documented separately by
Scramble: `Authorization` (Project API key) and `Idempotency-Key`
(required on every monetary mutation — replay the same key to get
the cached response without re-charging).

channel.description:
The channel the customer will pay through. The Core
routes the call to whichever payment provider is
configured for this channel on the calling Project —
the caller never names a provider directly.

amount.description:
The amount to charge, expressed in the smallest
indivisible unit of the currency — cents for USD/EUR,
centimes for XAF. The decimal-to-minor conversion is the
caller's responsibility. `100000` means 1000.00 in the
currency's major unit.

currency.description:
The ISO 4217 three-letter code of the currency. The
provider configured for the chosen `channel` must
support it — otherwise the request fails with a
422 `unsupported-currency` error before reaching the
payment network.

reason.description:
A short label for the payment, shown to the customer on
the hosted page and forwarded to the provider as the
transaction description. Max 255 characters. Not echoed
back in the API response — keep your own copy if you
need it later.

customer_phone_number.description:
The customer's phone number in international format
(E.164, e.g. `+2376XXXXXXXX`). Forwarded to the
provider so USSD prompts and OTP codes reach the right
line on mobile-money channels. Optional — providers that
need it for their flow will reject the request if it's
missing.

customer_name.description:
The customer's display name. Optional. Forwarded to the
provider and rendered on the hosted payment page where
the provider supports it.

customer_email.description:
The customer's email. Optional. Forwarded to the
provider for receipt delivery where supported. Not
persisted by the Core — the Core never holds customer
PII; whatever the provider does with it is the
provider's responsibility.

customer_lang.description:
A BCP-47 language tag for the customer's locale
(`fr`, `en`, `fr-CM`...). Forwarded to the provider so
the hosted payment page is rendered in the right
language. Optional — providers fall back to their
default when missing.

anyOf.description:
How the payment starts. `payin` is the synchronous,
app-driven flow: the Core returns immediately with a
transaction reference and the caller drives the
customer through their own UX. `paylink` is the
hosted-link flow: the Core returns a URL and the caller
redirects the customer there. If omitted, the
provider default applies (typically `payin`).

return_url.description:
Where to send the customer's browser after they
complete (or cancel) the payment on the
provider-hosted page. Best-effort: this is
browser-side only and may never fire (closed tab,
disabled JS, captive portal). For a reliable
server-to-server signal, use `callback_url` instead.

wallet_recipient_external_ref.description:
Optional. The external reference of the wallet to
credit automatically when this payment reaches a
successful terminal state. When present, the credit
happens in the same database transaction as the
payment confirmation — no separate API call needed,
no window for race conditions. When absent, the
payment is a pure collection: the money is held by the
Core but no wallet is credited. The value must match a
wallet owned by the calling Project; the request fails
with a 422 `wallet-project-mismatch` otherwise.

callback_url.description:
Where the Core POSTs the server-to-server notification
when the payment reaches a terminal state. This is the
reliable channel — use it to update your own order
state, release stock, send a confirmation email, etc.
The body is JSON and signed with HMAC-SHA256 (headers
`X-Signature`, `X-Timestamp`); the secret is returned
in the initiation response and never again, so store
it at registration time. Distinct from `return_url`:
this is server-to-server, `return_url` is browser-side.
